info.html:
LED Downlights are the most popular for residential and commercial lighting. Installing downlights in homes gives bright lighting with low running costs. Nowadays, there are many options to consider to achieve brightness and aesthetics of the room appearance according to your preferences.

Most downlights now come standard with a 3 colour (tri-colour) selectable switch. They give you the option of warm (3000 Kelvin), natural (4000K), and bright white or daylight (5000K). Some lights will also offer up to 6000K, although this is not recommended. Standard LED downlights can be very useful in areas requiring bright, even lighting to fill a space or room. However, a problem with this is achieving coverage; they use a white transparent diffuser that gives a wide spread of light and, unfortunately, causes glare and can create an uncomfortable environment.

Greenhse's new 10W LED downlight range is the most popular, with many different options to create the perfect lighting environment — from a standard (3 colour switchable) to low glare downlights, Smart full colour (RGBW), Smart CCT (2700–5700K), all with the same look and feel.

Architectural downlights in Perth incorporate low glare lenses or deep reflectors to provide lighting without the discomfort of glare. This type of lighting also provides more direct lighting, which enables areas and features to be highlighted. This creates a better ambience and mood.

Older-design tri-colour lights are harder to adjust compared to the new ones. The new LED downlights are smart and therefore adjustable — wider beam and low glare downlights output colour can now be controlled with a wide colour temperature range and brightness options using a smart device, and are Amazon Alexa and Google Home compatible.

Shop the best designer LED lighting in Perth — explore our most extensive residential and commercial lighting options. This exclusive collection is online or available in our Ellenbrook showroom to enable you to create the perfect lighting environment.

info.html:
A good ceiling fan does more than cool a room in summer — reversing the blade direction in winter pushes warm air (which naturally rises) back down, helping heating work more efficiently and cutting running costs year-round.

Modern DC-motor fans use a fraction of the power of older AC motors, run near silently, and offer far finer speed control — most of our range includes an integrated LED light kit too, so one fitting covers both airflow and illumination for the room.

Look for the right blade span and mounting drop for your ceiling height — low-profile (hugger) mounts suit standard ceilings, while extended rods suit high or raked ceilings, and outdoor-rated (damp/wet-location) fans are available for alfresco areas and patios.

info.html:
Every 12V/24V LED strip needs a transformer (driver) to step mains power down to a safe, steady low-voltage supply — get the sizing wrong and strips run dim, flicker, or fail early. Our range covers a wide spread of wattages so a single run, a whole room, or a multi-zone install can all be matched to the right unit rather than over- or under-powering it.

Controllers sit between the transformer and the strip, giving you dimming, colour changing (RGB/RGBW) or colour-temperature control (CCT) depending on what your strip supports. Options range from simple on/off and dimming remotes through to smart, app- and voice-controlled units for Alexa- and Google Home-compatible setups.

IP-rated, Australian-certified units are included throughout the range for damp areas, outdoor runs and bathrooms, alongside standard indoor-only drivers for cost- sensitive indoor jobs.

Not sure what pairs with your strip? Use the Strip Light Finder or the Lighting Layout App above, or call our Perth-based team on (08) 9297 2969and we'll spec the transformer and controller for you.

info.html:
Classrooms, offices and commercial fit-outs generally follow a lighting standard (such as AS/NZS 1680) covering minimum illuminance and glare control — recessed ceiling grid panels are the standard fitting because they sit flush in a T-bar ceiling and spread light evenly with low glare across a whole room.

Panel sizes are built to match standard ceiling grid modules (600×600mm and 600×1200mm are the most common), so replacing old fluorescent troffers is usually a straight swap without modifying the ceiling.

Larger fit-outs often add scene or zone control — grouping banks of lights to a wall keypad or a whiteboard/AV scene — so a room can switch between full light, presentation mode, or off without touching every switch individually.

info.html:
High bay lights are built for ceilings roughly 6m and above — warehouses, factories, gyms and large workshops — where a fixture needs to throw enough lumens straight down to properly light a floor from a long way up. Below that height, a low bay or standard fitting is usually the better (and cheaper) choice.

The round "UFO" design is the most common shape, using a wide heatsink to keep the LEDs cool over long duty cycles — important at height, where getting up to replace a fitting isn't a five-minute job. Linear high bays are also available for aisles and racking runs where a longer, narrower spread suits the space better.

Look for a high CRI and daylight-matched output for factory and warehouse floors where colour accuracy and glare control matter, and pair with a motion sensor or contactor control to cut running costs in areas that aren't occupied constantly.

Industrial spaces put real demands on a light fitting — dust, moisture, wash-down cleaning, vibration and long duty cycles all shorten the life of a fitting that isn't built for it. This range covers the sealed, heavy-duty fittings made to handle that environment rather than a standard commercial fitting pushed past its limits.

Vapor-tight (IP65+) fixtures with a gasket-sealed lens and toggle-clamp latches are the standard choice for coolrooms, wash-down areas and workshops where dust or moisture is a constant. Impact-resistant polycarbonate lenses hold up better than glass around moving equipment and forklifts.

Where colour accuracy matters — quality control, food prep, paint or print work — look for a higher CRI rating; where it's just about safe, reliable coverage on a factory floor, standard output fittings paired with a pushbutton or contactor control keep things simple.

Batten lights are the practical workhorse of LED fittings — a single linear housing that surface-mounts straight to a ceiling or wall, with no recess or cavity needed. That makes them the standard choice for garages, workshops, warehouses, carports and stairwells.

Modern LED battens run cooler and use a fraction of the power of the fluorescent tubes they replace, with instant-on brightness and no flicker or hum. Weatherproof (IP-rated) options are available for carports, alfresco areas and other exposed locations, alongside standard indoor units for workshops and garages.

Sizes typically run from around 0.6m up to 2.4m, so a run of battens can cover a single bench or a full warehouse aisle — link multiple fittings end to end for continuous runs without extra switches or cabling.

info.html:
A star light (or "star ceiling") kit runs thin fiber-optic strands from a single light-engine driver, through a ceiling, to end points that appear as individual twinkling stars — the fiber carries only light, not electricity, so there's no heat or wiring at each star point.

Kit size is driven by how many fiber strands (stars) and how much ceiling area you're covering — larger rooms or denser starfields need a higher-output driver and more strands. RGBW driver units add colour-changing and twinkle effects on top of a plain steady-white starfield.

Most kits are installed during a ceiling fit-out (fibers run above the ceiling lining before it's closed up), so it's worth planning a star ceiling early in a build or renovation rather than retrofitting afterwards.

Track lighting puts several independently-aimed heads on a shared power rail — each head swivels and rotates on its own, so a single track can wash a whole wall, spotlight a few feature pieces, or do both at once without extra wiring.

Heads and track connectors from the same system generally aren't interchangeable across brands, so it's worth sticking to one system for a run rather than mixing — check connector type before adding heads to an existing track.

Linear fittings suit a continuous run instead of individual points — under cabinetry, along a hallway, or recessed into a ceiling channel — and can usually be linked end to end to cover longer distances from a single power feed.

Security cameras and motion sensors work best when they're planned alongside your lighting, not bolted on afterwards — a camera pointed straight into a floodlight or a sensor tucked out of its own light's beam both undercut what they're there for.

Look for built-in infrared (IR) illuminators on cameras for usable night vision without relying on a separate light, and check detection range and angle on PIR sensors against the actual area you want covered — a narrow-angle sensor on a wide driveway will miss most of what walks through it.

Wired and Wi-Fi options both feature in this range — wired is more reliable for a permanent install, while Wi-Fi units are quicker to add or reposition without running new cable.
